function: Joint device activity detection and channel estimation, as sparse recovery of the effective device-BS channel matrix, in IRS-assisted grant-free massive access (p. 4-5).
system: Uplink grant-free mMTC: BS with 8-antenna ULA, 500 single-antenna devices, 4 passive reflecting IRS panels of 64 elements each, S-band (p. 3, 11, 13).
method: Unfolded ISTA and AMP networks (HISTA-Net, HAMP-Net) with DnCNN denoiser and dual attention; supervised alternating layer-by-layer training with NMSE loss (p. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh multipath fading with array steering vectors, 50,000 training samples at SNR 15-25 dB; Rician channels (factor 8 dB) for one extra test (p. 4, 11, 14).
test_conditions: Trained on Rayleigh, SNR 15-25 dB, random device types; tested versus SNR, pilots, activity probability, and on Rician channels without retraining (p. 11-14).
baselines: Classical: OMP, GMMV-AMP. Learned: PDNN, MMV-LAMP, JADCE, LISTA, DA-RLAMP (authors' earlier work) (p. 12-14).
metrics: NMSE of channel estimation, activity error probability (AEP), number of correctly detected active devices, running time (p. 11-14).
complexity: Table IV: running time (HAMP-Net 0.996 s, HISTA-Net 0.859 s) and order of complexity of each network (p. 14).
q1_support: p. 4: "We employ a multipath fading channel model"; custom Rayleigh simulator (p. 14), no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "During the estimation phase, all the links are replaced to Rician channels" after training on Rayleigh (Fig. 10).
q3_support: p. 12: "outperform the model driven networks and CS algorithms"; classical OMP, GMMV-AMP; learned PDNN, MMV-LAMP, JADCE; NMSE and AEP in Fig. 6.
q4_support: p. 15: "The running time and the computational complexity of the schemes are shown in Table IV"; Table IV on p. 14 gives times and O() orders.
q5_support: p. 11: "we generate 50, 000 independent complex datasets"; self-generated simulated data, no link to code or data anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 2: the main metric is the NMSE of channel estimation, activity error probability is secondary. Tables III and IV were read from the page images (p. 11, 14). q2 rests only on the Rayleigh to Rician test (p. 14); the sweeps over pilots and activity are not counted because the paper says that configuration parameters remain fixed during training and deployment (p. 13-14). Baseline code of other authors is used, own code not released.
